author: Old Dominion News
title: Joe Sheridan receives Atlantic 10 postgraduate scholarship for Richmond
text:
University of Richmond midfielder Joe Sheridan was named the school’s recipient of the Atlantic 10’s postgraduate scholarship, according to a May 27 announcement. The award is given annually to one student-athlete from each of the conference’s 14 member institutions and supports advanced academic or professional studies after graduation.
Sheridan, who majors in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology with a 3.9 GPA, is the only men’s lacrosse player among this year’s honorees. He helped lead the Spiders to one of their most successful seasons in program history in 2026, earning recognition as Atlantic 10 Midfielder of the Year, a spot on the All-Academic Team, and an All-American selection.
The Atlantic 10 Postgraduate Scholarship recognizes student-athletes who distinguish themselves academically and athletically while demonstrating character and leadership within their communities. The group of recipients this year includes six female and eight male student-athletes from seven different sports, posting an average GPA of 3.816—the highest since expanding to fourteen recipients.
Over the past decade, more than $612,000 has been awarded through this program to support former student-athletes’ full-time postgraduate or professional study. Currently, $42,000 is distributed annually across conference schools for this purpose.
A-10 Commissioner Dan Leibovitz said, “I would like to congratulate our outstanding group of student-athletes. Each recipient of our Postgraduate Scholarship has demonstrated excellence both in competition and in the classroom. As part of our ongoing commitment to supporting student-athletes, the Atlantic 10 is proud to assist with their postgraduate studies. We look forward to following the future successes of these 14 deserving honorees.”
